Hi Sven / Anna,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to understand NordBank's high-level use cases and the regulatory constraints you're working under. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the key points and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: customer support automation + document summarization for EU retail operations.
- Data residency requirement: EU-only at rest and in transit for PII and transaction metadata.
- Preferred deployment model: exploring Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) or Private VPC/on-prem for full data control. Hosted API is attractive for speed-to-prod but we need clarity on cross-region routing and EU-only guarantees.

Open questions we agreed to answer:
1) Which deployment modes can guarantee EU-only data residency and routing (no egress to US)?
2) Region availability timeline for Dedicated and Private in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Amsterdam (eu-west-1).
3) Impact to latency and cost between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your expected throughput (~30 rps, mixed short/long contexts).

Next steps (owners):
- Lauren: Share a short deployment matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) that highlights residency guarantees, typical SLA/latency, and estimated cost ranges. Will attach by EOD. (attachment: deployment-matrix.xlsx)
- Aditya: Follow up with tech details about cross-region routing and whether Hosted API ever routes tokens outside EU for processing.
- Sven/Anna: Send any procurement redline or procurement contact for next steps if we land on Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: deployment-matrix.xlsx (draft), nordbank-data-residency-qa.docx (sample answers)

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Sven / Anna — adding a few technical clarifications based on the infra side; happy to schedule a short tech sync if helpful.

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API (EU regions): When you use our EU-hosted endpoints (e.g., eu-central-1 or eu-west-1), inference compute and ephemeral caches are kept within that region. We do not route inference traffic to non-EU regions unless a customer explicitly configures multi-region fallbacks or uses cross-region archives. For customers with strict EU-only requirements we recommend pinning to an EU endpoint + disabling cross-region fallback in the routing policy.

- Cross-region failover & Dedicated: Dedicated pools can be region-pinned. We support automatic failover rules that remain within the regional scope you choose (e.g., primary eu-central-1, failover eu-west-1). Failover to non-EU regions is only used if expressly configured for cost/latency reasons.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): VPC-managed Private deployments in EU regions typically take 4–6 weeks (provisioning, network peering, KMS integration). On-prem deployments vary widely — simple appliance-style setups are 6–10 weeks depending on customer infra, audit windows, and network/firewall adjustments. We can provide a deployment-runbook with a breakdown of tasks and typical durations.

- Latency / cost: Hosted is fastest to get started and generally lowest operational overhead; Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale and guarantees reserved capacity; Private gives the most control (no shared infra) but has higher fixed setup costs and slightly higher median latency depending on customer networking. I can add a small table to the attachment showing sample latency/cost for 30 rps.

I'll attach a short technical appendix to the deck — let me know if you want a deeper session with our Solutions Engineering team.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
